The gem.wiki narrative is a near-verbatim paraphrase of that EPC page (identical 'crosses between Namak Lake and Howz-e Soltan Lake', 'rugged and swampy/lacustrine terrains', 'does not intersect the South-North Corridor', 'pig-launcher and LBV stations'). No INDEPENDENT source names a 'Kuh Sefid–Charmshahr' pipeline: exhaustive EN + Farsi searches (Shana, Mehr, NIGC, Wikipedia, OGJ, GulfPub) return only the iranertebat page and GEM itself. GulfPub PE World Map (49 Iran gas features incl. IGAT 1-11, offshore, cross-border) has NO Kuh Sefid, NO Charmshahr, NO Qom->Tehran 56in feature — no counterpart, which for a supposedly-operating 56in trunk near Tehran is itself an existence flag. The name is GEM-coined from the EPC project's two endpoints, not an official pipeline name. CRITICAL: the sole source could not be cited — scripts/url_verifier.py fails it repeatedly with ConnectTimeout (site appears geoblocked/sanctions-blocked from US infra), so per the standing rules there is NO verifier-passing reference for any field on this row. The physical work described (a 56in EPC line built across the Qom-Tehran salt-lake corridor) is plausibly real per the contractor, but as a standalone named 'operating pipeline' it is single-source and now unverifiable. Strong secondary suspicion it is a construction segment of a larger national trunk feeding Tehran/Rey rather than an independent pipeline (see duplicate note).

validity.researcher_notes: A 45 km, 56-inch line running north from the Qom area (Kuh Sefid, near Howz-e Soltan) into south Tehran (Charmshahr industrial town, Rey) is exactly the profile of a segment of a national gas trunk reinforcing Tehran, not a standalone pipeline. Candidates in-roster: P6026 North–Northeast Gas Pipeline (?->Tehran, 35km) but that is 48in not 56in; IGAT-8 (P0447, 56in, Parsian->Qom) which could plausibly continue Qom->Tehran. No confident geometry/PID match was established and GulfPub offers no counterpart, so this is flagged as a relabel/segment-double-count RISK, not a proven duplicate. Iran's IGAT trunk series is known to be split into EPC-contract segments that get double-counted; this row has the hallmarks (EPC-contract-derived name, single EPC source, mid-corridor endpoints).

validity.recommendation: Change Owner/Operator from NIOC to NIGC (Iranian Gas Transmission Co / IGTC) pending confirmation, and clear/repair FuelSource. Do not apply without an independent citable source.
validity.researcher_notes: Two attribution problems. (1) Owner1 = 'National Iranian Oil Co' (NIOC 100%). Domestic gas TRANSMISSION in Iran is owned/operated by the National Iranian Gas Company (NIGC) through the Iranian Gas Transmission Company (IGTC), not NIOC — NIOC is upstream oil/gas production. For a domestic Qom->Tehran distribution-feed trunk, NIGC/IGTC is the expected owner. (GulfPub labels many Iran gas trunks 'NIOC' by its own convention, so it does not settle this.) (2) FuelSource = 'Kuh Sefid' is mis-derived: Kuh Sefid ('White Mountain') is the START VILLAGE in Qom province, not a gas field/production source. There is no 'Kuh Sefid' gas field feeding this line; the gas is national-grid gas arriving via the IGAT system. FuelSource should be blanked or set to the feeding trunk, not the endpoint town. Could not obtain a verifier-passing source to stage the corrected owner, so this is flagged, not filled.

routes.corridor_desc: Per the sole descriptive source, the 56in line starts at Kuh Sefid village in Qom Province and runs NORTH between Howz-e Soltan salt lake (to the west) and the larger Namak Lake (to the east), through rugged/swampy lacustrine terrain, into Tehran Province, ending at the Charmshahr industrial town area south of Tehran (Rey/Kahrizak). This is a real, well-defined geographic corridor (the Qom-Tehran salt-lake gap along the Tehran-Qom axis), so the CORRIDOR is defensible even though endpoint coordinates are approximate: Charmshahr Industrial Town (~35.43N, 51.38E, sourced as ~12km from Tehran) is a real named place; Howz-e Soltan (~34.94N, 50.95E) and Namak Lake (~34.75N, 51.5E) are well-known landmarks the line passes between. Kuh Sefid village exact coordinates could NOT be sourced — left null; it lies in Qom Province near the south end of this gap, roughly 45km south of Charmshahr, consistent with the stated 45km length. Loosely bounded start; tight corridor.
routes.researcher_notes: Endpoints/corridor established from the single (unverifiable, uncitable) iranertebat description plus independent geography of the named landmarks (Howz-e Soltan, Namak Lake, Charmshahr Industrial Town). summary: P6027 CONCERN (existence+duplicate+attribution+spec): sole support is one uncitable/geoblocked EPC portfolio page (iranertebat), GEM-coined name, no independent corroboration and no GulfPub counterpart; likely a 56in IGAT/Tehran-feed segment mislabeled as standalone; Owner NIOC likely wrong (NIGC/IGTC) and FuelSource 'Kuh Sefid' is the start village not a field; corridor (Qom->Charmshahr between Howz-e Soltan & Namak Lake) is defensible but suggested route accuracy stays low.
